patch_description: Best known approach is the sequential Steiner-like discount framework (Gen 10: cost 756): process destinations one at a time, and once an edge is paid for by an earlier destination, subsequent destinations see it as nearly free (cost 0.001), encouraging shared-tree transfers and eliminating redundant parallel transfers. Key parameters to improve: (1) destination ordering — I replace static ascending-cost ordering with greedy dynamic ordering: at each step, choose the destination whose discounted path cost gives the largest savings relative to its original shortest-path cost (maximizing immediate edge reuse), a classic greedy Steiner-tree heuristic; (2) discount magnitude 0.001 (keep); (3) capacity fallback — no throughput penalty since it hurt in other variants. Unreachable destinations are handled gracefully with empty partition paths. Per-edge append format `[s, t, G[s][t]]` for all partitions kept exactly as in the proven framework.
